cfg.raw_spark: A tool for physiotherapists in small practices because every time an insurer rejects a claim over a mismatched treatment code the physio has to dig the original referral letter out of one system, cross-check the code list in a second system, rewrite the claim line by line in the insurer portal, and then remember to follow up two weeks later to see if it went through this time, and nobody in a two-person practice has a spare afternoon for that every single week.
cfg.grapeRel: my physio, runs a two-person practice

answers.m2: Last Tuesday an insurer rejected a claim over a mismatched code, and Ilse spent her lunch break digging out the referral letter and rewriting the claim line by line in the portal.
answers.m3: My friend Jordan, who runs a small dental practice, told me last month he started keeping a printed code cheat-sheet after a similar rejection.
answers.m4: Priya, a massage therapist I met at a conference, keeps a folder of past approved claims to copy from. For her the pain is the follow-up timing, the coding part is fine.
answers.m5: Ilse uses the insurer's own portal to resubmit claims, but it has no way to flag which codes were previously rejected, so the same mismatch can happen twice.
answers.m6: "I don't have a spare afternoon for this every week," she said after the Tuesday one.
answers.m7: Owen works purely on a cash-pay basis with no insurance billing at all. Claim rejections never happen to him because there are no claims to submit.
